subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw reject non-text-output models when they are configured as chat/session models, or add first-class output-modality metadata and runtime support for image/video output?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but the choice changes public config semantics and provider/tool ownership, so automation should not pick it from source inspection alone.

options.title: Reject unsupported chat output now
options.body: Add a clear diagnostic for image/video-output models selected as chat/session models and direct users to `image_generate` or `video_generate` until first-class support exists.

options.title: Add output-modality support
options.body: Extend config/catalog metadata and runtime/channel rendering so selected models can intentionally produce image/video outputs in session flow.

options.title: Docs-only clarification
options.body: Document that media generation must use the generation tools while leaving current custom-provider behavior unchanged, accepting continued runtime confusion.

recommendation.title: Reject unsupported chat output now
recommendation.body: Add a clear diagnostic for image/video-output models selected as chat/session models and direct users to `image_generate` or `video_generate` until first-class support exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses provider/model config, docs, and media-generation direction where recent history shows repeated ownership.
